newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Friday were at a standstill ahead of the afternoon USDA Cattle-On-Feed report, feedlot sources said.
The monthly report was expected to show active placements of cattle into feedlots during March, they said. Release was set for 1400 CDT/1900 GMT.

Average pre-report analysts' estimates pegged March placements at 103.3 percent of a year ago from a range of 100.5 to 107.0. April 1 on-feed estimates averaged 107.6 percent of a year ago and March marketings estimates averaged 100.6.
Thin packer bids at $67.00 to $68.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $69.00 to $70.00, sources said.
Most of this week's showlists were depleted, which meant there would be minimal carryover into next week, they said.
The bulk of fed cattle this week sold at $69.00, up $2.00 from the majority of last week's sales, supported by strong beef demand the past two weeks.
Beef demand was powered by retail bookings for month-end outdoor grilling features, market sources said.
However, fed cattle prices next week could be softer if retail beef demand slows, they said.
USDA near midday Friday said beef cut-out values slipped $0.23 to $0.45 per cwt on 161 loads of fabricated cuts sold.
